title: Save Me!
statement: It asks for the fewest operations, each replacing a_i or a_{i+1} by a_i XOR a_{i+1}, until some element is zero (else -1), for n ≤ 100 values below 2^25 under 16 MB. Operations are invertible, so -1 iff the values are GF(2)-independent. A zero-XOR subset spanning [l, r] costs r−l plus skipped elements, at most 49; a 2^25 XOR DP exceeds memory, so meet-in-the-middle splits paths at half cost.
